chunking.title: Chunking
chunking.summary: Each document is split by paragraphs.
items: Paragraphs of up to about 800 characters become one fragment.
Longer paragraphs are split by sentences into blocks of about 500 characters.
Each fragment keeps the document name so it can be cited.

search.title: Keyword search (BM25)
items: Compares the words in your question with each fragment (BM25: word frequency weighted by how rare the word is).
Only the 5 best-scoring fragments are sent to the model.
It is lexical search: use words that appear in the documents. Semantic search (embeddings) is configured in your project.

answer.title: Answers with citations
items: The server always adds three rules for the model: answer only from the fragments, cite the source of each fact and say “I couldn’t find that information in the uploaded documents.” when it is not there.
Each citation [n] opens the exact fragment and the document it came from.

models.summary: GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o or GPT-4 Turbo.
items: You pick the model above; the server only accepts these three.
Without an API key, the demo switches to extractive mode: it shows the retrieved fragments with their citation, without writing an answer.

howItWorks.title: How this demo audits
howItWorks.intro: This is exactly what the demo engine does with each invoice. Everything else is configured in your project.

s1.title: PDF reading
s1.desc: The server extracts the PDF text. Scanned PDFs (images) are not read in this demo.

s2.title: AI extraction
s2.desc: The procedures table is read with patterns (code, description, quantity and amounts). An OpenAI language model (GPT-4o mini) extracts the invoice number, patient, ICD-10 diagnosis and authorization.

s3.title: Fee schedule and rules
s3.desc: Each CUPS code is compared against the sample fee schedule. If the billed amount exceeds the tariff, a denial for the difference is proposed.

s4.title: Model proposal
s4.desc: A second OpenAI model (GPT-4o) reviews the data and drafts a proposal: amount to pay, rationale and whether human review is needed.

s5.title: Auditor decision
s5.desc: You confirm, adjust or discard each denial with a note. The server recalculates the totals and you can download the report as CSV or PDF.

rules.r3: Rule codes (such as 202) are internal to the demo; in your project they are mapped to Colombia's current Single Manual of Returns, Denials and Responses.

how.margin: Margin = (sales − cost) ÷ sales, by line, comparing the period with the same months of {prevYear}. Lines are sorted from the largest drop to the largest increase.
how.customersDown: For each customer I compare the period’s sales with the same months of {prevYear} (only customers who were already buying) and sort by the difference in pesos.
how.cash8: This is week 8 of the 13-week cash flow in Finance: it starts from cash at cut-off ({date}: {start}) and adds projected collections and subtracts payments week by week.
how.cityGoal: Target for each city or site = its sales in the same months of {prevYear} + {goal}%. Attainment = sales ÷ target.
how.overdue: I add up open invoices more than 60 days past due at the end of the period and group them by customer.
how.forecastSeasonal: Each month = sales of the same month last year × growth of the last 3 months vs. the same months last year ({growth}). The 80% band comes from the error this method had in the months already known (deviation {sigma}).
how.forecastTrend: Linear trend of the last months with data. The 80% band comes from the deviation from that trend ({sigma}).

refund.title: How to process a refund or a duplicate charge
refund.body: Check in the payment gateway that there are two approved transactions. If the charge is duplicated, request the reversal from the payments panel: the money returns to the payment method in 3 to 8 business days, depending on the bank. Record the request number in the ticket and let the customer know.
refund.reply: Hi {name}, we confirmed the duplicate charge and have already requested the refund. The money returns to your payment method in 3 to 8 business days, depending on your bank. We’ll email you the receipt.

einvoice.title: I didn’t receive my electronic invoice
einvoice.body: The electronic invoice is emailed to the registered address when it is issued. If it doesn’t arrive, check the spam folder and confirm the registered email is correct. The PDF and XML can be downloaded from “My invoices” at any time. If the email is wrong, update it and resend the invoice.
einvoice.reply: Hi {name}, your electronic invoice is sent to the email address you registered, so please also check your spam folder. You can download the PDF and XML from “My invoices” anytime. If you prefer, we can resend it to another email.

pse.title: Pending or declined PSE payments
pse.body: A PSE payment can stay pending for up to 30 minutes while the bank confirms it. If the bank declines it, no money is debited. If the customer sees the debit and the payment shows as declined, the bank reverses the money automatically in 1 to 3 business days.
pse.reply: Hi {name}, a PSE payment can stay pending for up to 30 minutes while your bank confirms it. If the bank declined it and you see the debit, the reversal is automatic within 1 to 3 business days. If it doesn’t show up, write to us with the receipt.

password.title: Reset your password or access code
password.body: On the sign-in screen choose “Forgot your password?”. A link is sent to the registered email, valid for 15 minutes. If the SMS verification code doesn’t arrive, check the signal and that the registered number is correct; a new code can be requested every 60 seconds.
password.reply: Hi {name}, on the sign-in screen choose “Forgot your password?” and you’ll get a link by email, valid for 15 minutes. If the SMS code doesn’t arrive, you can request a new one every 60 seconds. If it still doesn’t work, reply here and we’ll help you.

orderStatus.title: Order status and tracking number
orderStatus.body: The tracking number is emailed when the order leaves the warehouse and also appears in “My orders”. Shipping to major cities takes 2 to 4 business days, and to other towns 4 to 7 business days.
orderStatus.reply: Hi {name}, you can check your order status under “My orders” with your tracking number, which is also emailed to you when the order leaves the warehouse. Shipping to major cities takes 2 to 4 business days. If it doesn’t arrive within that time, reply here and we’ll look into it.

address.title: Change the delivery address
address.body: The address can be changed as long as the order has not left the warehouse. Confirm the full new address (neighborhood, apartment and city) and update it on the order. If it has already shipped, request the change from the carrier, which may charge a fee.
address.reply: Hi {name}, we can change the address as long as your order hasn’t left the warehouse. Send us the full address (neighborhood, apartment and city) and we’ll update it right away.

returns.title: Exchanges and returns
returns.body: For online purchases, customers have a right of withdrawal within 5 business days after delivery (Colombian Consumer Statute, Law 1480 of 2011). Size exchanges are requested in “My orders” within 30 days after delivery, with the item unused and with its tags.
returns.reply: Hi {name}, you can request the exchange in “My orders” within 30 days after delivery, with the item unused and with its tags. If you’d rather return it, you have a right of withdrawal within 5 business days after delivery.

slowInternet.title: Slow or intermittent internet: troubleshooting
slowInternet.body: Before escalating: 1) check whether there is a reported outage in the area; 2) ask the customer to unplug the modem for 30 seconds; 3) test the speed over a cable; 4) check how many devices are connected. If the internet light is still red, escalate to level 2 support.
slowInternet.reply: Hi {name}, let’s check it together: unplug the modem for 30 seconds and plug it back in. If the internet light is still red, let us know and we’ll escalate the case to technical support right away.

visit.title: Schedule or reschedule a technician visit
visit.body: Technician visits are scheduled in a morning slot (8:00 to 12:00) or an afternoon slot (14:00 to 18:00), Monday to Saturday. The technician confirms by WhatsApp one hour before. If the visit doesn’t happen because of the company, it is not charged.
visit.reply: Hi {name}, we can schedule the visit in the morning slot (8:00 to 12:00) or the afternoon slot (14:00 to 18:00), Monday to Saturday. The technician will confirm by WhatsApp one hour before. Which slot works for you?

cancelPlan.title: Cancel or pause a plan
cancelPlan.body: Before cancelling, offer an alternative: switching to a cheaper plan or pausing the service for up to 2 months. If the customer insists, file the cancellation request; it takes effect at the end of the billing cycle.
cancelPlan.reply: Hi {name}, before cancelling, we can move you to a cheaper plan or pause the service for up to 2 months at no cost. If you prefer to cancel, we’ll file your request and it will take effect at the end of your billing cycle.

overview.scopeTitle: What this demo does and does not do

does.0: Generates a post, ad copy and a carousel with AI (an OpenAI model called from KopTup's server) or, when AI is not available, with local templates, and tells you which one it used.
does.1: Lets you edit the text, checks it for accuracy alerts, saves drafts in this browser and exports them to CSV.
does.2: Creates 1200×627 images from templates, downloads the carousel as a PDF and captures a photo or video of any KopTup demo.
does.3: Adds UTM parameters to links so you can measure visits in your analytics.

doesNot.0: It does not connect to your LinkedIn account or post for you (simulated in the demo; in a custom project it can connect to the LinkedIn API if your company has approved access).
doesNot.1: It does not measure reach, clicks or followers: the preview shows no real reactions.
doesNot.2: It does not make up results: the texts include no client figures or testimonials; if you add a figure, it needs a source.

howItWorks.title: What is real in this demo
howItWorks.real: Calculated for real in your browser: the points for each purchase (base rule plus multipliers by category, day and channel), the balance as the sum of the points ledger, tiers, redemptions with coupons and checkout discounts, missions, referrals, fraud rules, allowed campaign hours, the cost simulator, the points liability and the CSV export. howItWorks.title: What is real in this demo
howItWorks.real: Everything is calculated in your browser: stock per store, taxes included in prices (19% VAT, 5% VAT, exempt or 8% consumption tax), points, change, tips, kitchen tickets, X and Z reports, cash count, commissions and the store console. Your sales and changes are saved only in this browser.
howItWorks.scanner: The “Scan” field accepts a real barcode scanner connected as a keyboard (USB or Bluetooth); if you don't have one, use the sample codes.
howItWorks.simulated: Simulated: sending the document to the DIAN (the CUDE is computed here with SHA-384, in test mode, and never leaves your browser), the card terminal, QR payments, the scale, printer and cash drawer, and sending the receipt by WhatsApp or email. The “Offline” button is a demo switch: it does not cut your connection.
howItWorks.project: In your project, the till installs as an app on a tablet or PC, stores sales on the device when the internet goes down and syncs them when it comes back, issues the electronic document through your authorized technology provider and connects to your card terminal, thermal printer, scanner, cash drawer and scale.

steps.1: Retail: press “Scan”, use a sample code and weigh a per-kilo product with “Read scale”.
steps.2: In the ticket, look up customer 300 123 4567, redeem 500 points and take a split payment: part cash, the rest by card or QR.
steps.3: Turn on “Offline”, make another sale (it is queued) and reconnect to see it sync.
steps.4: Restaurant: open a table in “Tables”, take the order with modifiers, send it to the kitchen and move the ticket forward in “Kitchen (KDS)”.
steps.5: In “X/Z reports” review sales by payment method and close the shift with a cash count; in “Stores” move stock between stores.
